summary: awesome-web-scraping is a curated awesome-list (not a library) containing 400+ categorized links to web scraping tools, libraries, and services across Python, JavaScript, Go, Ruby, PHP, and Java. It organizes resources by functional category: HTTP clients, scraping frameworks, HTML/XML parsers, browser automation, job queues, proxy/CAPTCHA services, content extraction, and auxiliary utilities. The repo is actively maintained (576 commits, last commit July 2026) with 7,992 stars and regular PR merges. It serves purely as a human-readable discovery index - no executable code, no API, no runtime integration possible.

findings.description: Provides categorized discovery of 400+ web scraping related tools across 6 languages. Categories include: HTTP clients (requests, httpx, aiohttp), scraping frameworks (Scrapy, Crawlee, Ruia, Colly), HTML parsers (lxml, BeautifulSoup, selectolax, parsel), browser automation (Playwright, Selenium, Puppeteer, Pyppeteer), job queues (Celery, RQ, Huey), proxy management, CAPTCHA solving, content extraction (newspaper, trafilatura, goose), and auxiliary tools (URL parsing, user-agent generation, date parsing, price parsing).

apiSurface: Not a library - no API surface. This is a curated markdown catalog (awesome-list) of web scraping tools, libraries, and services across multiple languages (Python, JavaScript, Go, Ruby, PHP, Java) plus CLI tools, manuals, and related resources. Users consume it by reading markdown files to discover tools.
integrationPoints: Reference-only integration for Veridian pipeline. Could be used during tool selection phase to evaluate candidates (e.g., compare Playwright vs Crawlee vs Botasaurus for browser automation; select httpx vs aiohttp for async HTTP; choose parsel vs selectolax for parsing). Not integrable into runtime pipeline - no code to import or call.
strengthsForVeridian: Excellent reference catalog for tool selection phase. Comprehensive coverage of Python ecosystem (most relevant for Veridian) including modern async tools (httpx, aiohttp, Crawlee, Playwright). Actively maintained with recent additions like Crawlee, Botasaurus, Wavexis. Well-organized categories map to pipeline stages (fetch → parse → queue → extract). No lock-in, no bloat - just curated knowledge.
weaknessesForVeridian: Zero runtime utility - cannot be imported, called, or composed into a pipeline. No quality signals beyond stars/links (no benchmark data, no compatibility matrices, no version guidance). Some entries are stale (Ghost.py, Spynner, PhantomJS-era tools). No programmatic access - must be read manually. Does not solve any pipeline problem directly.
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
